title: Buy Now Default Later
summary: How Money Works explains why BNPL companies struggle to profit despite rapid loan growth and merchant fees.

assertions.quote: Affirm lost nearly half a billion dollars last year
by now, pay later companies have started charging as much as 8% on sales to average retailers
after consumers started using buy now pay later services, they were 17 to 26% more likely to make a purchase
they are much younger than formal credit card users, spend more impulsively, and have purchasing power

verdicts.note: The user base does skew younger, but characterizing all of them as more impulsive is a broader generalization than the data cleanly supports.

assertions.quote: more than half of BNPL users took on these loans because it was the only way they could afford it
stretching out the period between purchase and actually needing money by more than 4 months

verdicts.note: A 2025 poll cited across several videos found about 40% of users had used one loan to make a payment on a different debt.
KC Fed endnote: some BNPL providers allow repayment by credit card but charge a convenience fee of up to 3% for doing so.
